question: What is the maximum grant I can get if I apply for grant-only support?
reference_answer: Up to EUR 2.5 million, and grant-only support can only be received once per company during Horizon Europe (2021-27).

question: If the EU gives us a grant, how much of the project do we still have to pay ourselves?
reference_answer: Up to 70% of eligible costs; the remaining 30% must be financed by the company from its own resources (p75).

question: How much money can the EIC invest in my startup, at least and at most?
reference_answer: Minimum EUR 1 million and maximum EUR 10 million; higher amounts are available under the EIC STEP Scale Up call.

question: We have about 400 employees. Can we still get just the grant, without giving up equity?
reference_answer: No. Small mid-caps (up to 499 employees) can only apply for investment-only support, or blended finance in exceptional cases for rapid scale-up.

question: How long should the innovation activities funded by the grant last?
reference_answer: Normally they should be completed within 24 months, but they can be longer in well justified cases.

question: What do I need to submit for the short proposal?
reference_answer: A short 12-page form, a pitch deck of up to ten slides (pdf) and a video pitch of up to three minutes with up to three core team members.

question: When are short proposals sent for evaluation?
reference_answer: They are batched on the first Tuesday of every month at 17:00 Brussels time.

question: How long does it take to get the result of a short proposal?
reference_answer: Approximately 4-6 weeks from the batching date.

question: Who decides if our first application passes, and how many of them need to approve it?
reference_answer: Four expert evaluators; at least three of the four must give a GO for the proposal to succeed.

question: What are the cut-off dates for submitting a full proposal in 2027?
reference_answer: 20 January 2027, 17 March 2027, 1 September 2027 and 4 November 2027 (17:00 Brussels time).

question: What is the page limit for the full proposal form?
reference_answer: A maximum of 20 pages.

question: What score does my full proposal need to be considered for an interview?
reference_answer: At least 4 out of 5 on each of the three award criteria and an overall score of at least 13 out of 15.

question: We've been rejected twice already. Is there a limit to how many times we can try again?
reference_answer: After three unsuccessful submissions (at any stage and for any type of support) a company cannot apply again under Horizon Europe.

question: Can a company from the United Kingdom apply to the EIC Accelerator?
reference_answer: Yes, but UK applicants can only request and receive grant-only funding.

question: How long is the interview with the EIC Jury and how is it structured?
reference_answer: At most 45 minutes: up to 10 minutes of presentation using the pitch deck and up to 35 minutes of questions and answers with the jury.

question: How many people from my company can join the online interview with the technology expert?
reference_answer: A maximum of three participants, and no consultants are allowed.

question: Does my short proposal video have to be in English?
reference_answer: No, it can be in any EU language and may include subtitles.

question: How much of my company will the EU own if they invest?
reference_answer: Minority stakes, generally between 10% and 20%.

question: How can the EIC Fund exit its investment in my company?
reference_answer: Exit routes may include IPOs, management buy-outs, secondary sales or liquidations, decided case by case with co-investors.

question: Does the EIC Fund expect other investors to invest alongside it?
reference_answer: Yes. For direct equity it seeks co-investment at least on a 1:1 matching basis, aiming for a leverage effect of 1:3 over the investment horizon.

question: Once we're selected, how long until the investment money actually comes through?
reference_answer: Usually between two and six months from the selection for funding.

question: Can the EIC Fund invest more than the amount I asked for?
reference_answer: Yes, by a flexibility amount of maximum EUR 2 million per proposal, if justified and if budget is available.

question: What do we get if our application scores well but we're not called to pitch to the jury?
reference_answer: You receive a Seal of Excellence (and a STEP Seal if submitted under a relevant challenge).

question: How much business coaching do I get after my short proposal is successful?
reference_answer: You can select an EIC business coach and receive up to 3 days of remote coaching, once per proposal.

question: The guide says I need TRL 6, but what TRL level does my innovation actually need to have reached when I apply?
reference_answer: It must have completed all aspects of TRL 5 (validation in a relevant environment); the Guide describes this as being at TRL 6 or above, and the grant funds TRL 6 to 8 activities.

question: For blended finance, what is the maximum grant, the maximum investment, and the maximum share of voting rights the EIC will take?
reference_answer: Grant up to about EUR 2.5 million (70% of eligible costs), investment from EUR 1 to 10 million, and a maximum of 25% of the voting shares.

question: After submitting my full proposal, when will I have the technology expert interview and when will I know if I am invited to the jury?
reference_answer: The online interview with the technology expert is about 3-4 weeks after the batching date, and the evaluation panel results come about 8-9 weeks after the batching date.

question: I run a UK startup. What type of funding can I get and how much at most?
reference_answer: UK applicants can only receive grant-only support, which is limited to a maximum of EUR 2.5 million.

question: If the jury does not fund my project, what do I receive and how can I use it to get money elsewhere?
reference_answer: A Seal of Excellence, which helps you get funding from other programmes; it only becomes operational if you consented to share your application data with other funding bodies when submitting.

question: Who evaluates my full proposal and what score do I need to reach the jury interview?
reference_answer: A technology expert and an evaluation panel of at least three experts; you need at least 4/5 per criterion and 13/15 overall.

question: If the EIC Fund invests, does my company's IP have to stay in Europe, and how will the EIC eventually exit?
reference_answer: The EIC Fund makes sure companies keep most of their value, including IP, in the EU or Associated Countries; exits are decided case by case and may be through IPOs, management buy-outs, secondary sales or liquidations.
